L23: 
L24: This is an upgrade of FHAW - RAF Ascension Island/ Wideawake Airfield.
L25: 
L26: Owned by the Brits. Run by the Americans. The main stuff that seems to come through here is big stuff on its way somewhere else. Fairly inevitable really.
L27: 
L28: This area is a right throwback to the start of the sim. The stock version still has no satellite image and the elevations come and go depending on their mood.
L29: The airport has been filled out with some details. Some buildings have been replaced, some added. Ground textures have been tarted up. Some light added.
L30: 
L31: This isn't premier league but it's an improvement on the utter blankness of the original.
L32: 
L33: The runway's gradients have been tweaked to try to match its famous hump. For some reason ATC only wants you to go to the wrong end of the runway.
L34: 
L35: Some hills have been returned as this half of the island is flat as a pancake in the original.
L36: A fuel truck is available for your thirst. You're gonna need it.
L37: 
L38: There are now two versions of this so click again to find them.
L39: V 1.7
L40: 
L41: Bends the airfield around the aerial image of the island found here - cite22†https://flightsim.to/file/64419/ascension-island-aerial-ground-image L42: 
L43: The aerial image is a right storage hog so you may not want it. I understand.
L44: Attempts to add more elevations. There's something seriously screwed with them here on the airfield side of the island. I sometimes see the correct ones for a couple of seconds and then they disappear again.
L45: 
L46: I think it's something to do with areas without a proper satellite image but I'm really not sure. If you get proper ones then I'm envious but this mod may not work with it. There will no doubt be weird lumps here and there and some that refuse to appear. So be it.
L47: Improves ground textures and details. Redesigns the taxi system to reflect the proper ground markings. Adds a helipad, though I've no idea where you'd fly to.
L48: 
L49: Adds a second version for all you new Vulcan owners that sort of looks like the 1982 version. I'm sure you're looking forward to flying for 16 hours over featureless water.

L35: Martinique Aimé Césaire International Airport (French: Aéroport international de Martinique-Aimé-Césaire, is the international airport of Martinique in the French West Indies. Located in Le Lamentin, a suburb of the capital Fort-de-France, it was opened in 1950 and renamed in 2007, after author and politician Aimé Césaire.
L36: When I first use MSFS I went to Martinique because I spent my childhood in this island. As my father was a pilot there I know pretty well the area, and I was a little disapointed about the airport area which was far from reality so I decided to fix that
L37: Originally I designed this scenery for my personal use, and then I decided to share it with others, et voila !!!!

L23: ## About this file
L24: 
L25: Cluj-Napoca International Airport (Traian Vuia Airport) is situated 3 km East of Cluj-Napoca, Romania, ICAO code LROP.
L26: 
L27:   * Hand crafted terminals, some buildings and the aprons (markings, taxiways...)
L28: 
L29: Unfortunately, because the default MSFS AIRAC database is not updated to the actual layout / procedures of the airport, you must manually configure the approach / departure procedures, including ILS FRQ and HDG.
L30: Fortunately, for those ones who have a NAVIGRAPH subscription, the AIRAC database is up to date.
L31: ## Installation
L32: 
L33: Extract the “luciancristea-lrcl” folder from the zip file to your Microsoft Flight Simulator “Community” folder.
L34: 
L35: Depending of your MSFS installation, you may find the “Community” folder:
L36: 
L37: Microsoft Store edition AND/OR Gamepass edition:
L38: 
L39: C:\Users\[YOUR USERNAME]\AppData\Local\Packages\Microsoft.FlightSimulator_\LocalCache\Packages\Community
L40: 
L41: Steam edition:
L42: 
L43: C:\Users\[YOUR USERNAME]\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft Flight Simulator\Packages\Community

L28: #### R. L. BRADSHAW INTERNATIONAL & VANCE W. AMORY INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT UPDATED SCENERY PACK PROJECT
L29: 
L30: [WORK IN PROGRESS]
L31: 
L32: DESCRIPTION:
L33: This is a scenery combo pack project for the R. L. Bradshaw International and Vance W. Amory International Airports on the Islands of St. Kitts & Nevis located in the Caribbean North-West of Antigua. Being a local on the Island of St. Kitts and a frequent Sim flyer since 2002 and after flying around in the default scenery for MSFS2020, I decided to take up the task of using/learning Developer Mode and update the Airport scenery and its surroundings close to IRL.
L34: It's still a work in progress here and there.  I'm still sorting out any bug/terrain formation issues I get from time to time after compiling. It's not perfect and I'm not 100% accurate but I try for at least 95%. :)
L35: 
L36: I've updated Nevis (TKPN - Vance W. Amory International Airport) as well after reaching some good headway with St.Kitts (TKPK). Though, still a work in progress as TKPN's parking lot behind has yet to be completed.
L37: If anyone who downloads these (specifically locals like myself who are frequent flight simmers or real life pilots who know the islands well) have any issues/comments/suggestions on how/where certain things are placed (or missing) feel free to connect with me here. I'm open to any suggestions to anything I may have missed while doing this project.
L38: 
L39: INSTALLATION:
L40: For previous users who downloaded earlier versions of this mod before v2.0, I recommend deleting the entire old folder from your Community folder before installing this version as to prevent seeing double objects in the scenery. This version now includes Nevis and thus the folder name had to be changed.
L41: Open and extract ''lexpro-tkpk_tkpn-updated-scenery-pack-project-v2.5.0zip'' (or the version name you choose to download) to your prefered location on your PC, then unZip and open the folder and copy both "R L Bradshaw Int_Updated_Scenery_Project" and "Vance W Amory Int_Updated_Scenery_Project" folders into where your Community folder is located, then start the sim and go to TKPK Bradshaw International or TKPN Vance Amory International. That's it!
L42: Each time I upload an updated version here, just replace the same "R L Bradshaw Int_Updated_Scenery_Project" folder or "Vance W Amory Int_Updated_Scenery_Project" folder in your Community folder to update the scenery. Make back ups to the old folders if necessary.
L43: (Please note, when choosing a parking space for departure, don't choose any single digit parking spaces numbered by themselves. Those are for the service vehicles to drive to if you have them enabled in your settings. You will be spawned in locations not meant for Airplanes. This is also the only way I found to manipulate these vehicles from annoyingly taxi on the same taxiway as the player but unforunately still park in your parking space)
L44: 
L45: 
L46: 
L47: DETAILED UPDATED FEATURES TO DEFAULT SCENERY (V2.5) - TKPN:
L48:                                           [COMING SOON]
L49: 
L50: 
L51: 
L52: DETAILED UPDATED FEATURES TO DEFAULT SCENERY (V2.5) - TKPK:
L53:   * - Updated and corrected taxiway markings and data for all aprons to how they look IRL [present day]
L54:   * - Updated taxiway Alpha textures to a concrete look [IRL they recently repaved taxiway Alpha]
L55:   * - Corrected terraforming and elevation for taxiway Alpha [IRL it's not completely flat and not on the same level as the runway]
L56:   * - Corrected actual position of windsock
L57:   * - Added extra anntenas where they are located IRL
L58:   * - Added an extra row of PAPI lights [IRL there are 2 different sets of the lights. My guess is that they upgraded them and left the old ones behind the new ones.]
L59:   * - Added some additional scenery details here and there.
L60:   * - Added the words "Welcome to SKB" in the middle of the solar panels like they are IRL.
L61:   * - Added back taxiway lights that were removed because of previous sim/world updates.
L62:   * - Corrected threshold markings for Runway 07/25 to present day look.
L63:   * -  Added a building and a few scenery objects together that simulates where our covid-19 testing station is presently on the main apron
L64: DETAILED UPDATED FEATURES TO DEFAULT SCENERY (V1.0) - TKPN:
L65:   * - Started from scratch and deleted everything except the default terminal building.
L66:   * - I havn't used Blender in very long while, so I stratigically placed very specific scenery objects from the sim library around the default building to try match the design structure IRL.
L67:   * - Made some corrections to the surrounding terrain of the Airport [This was somewhat challenging to get it right]
L68:   * -  Added runway/lights, PAPI lights, aprons, taxi lights, taxi ways, ''wear n' tear'' textures and ground markings. [The parking names/letters may not be accurate so I just used my imagination]
L69:   * -  Corrected location of Windsock
L70:   * - Added a light above the Windsock
L71:   * - Added the control tower with a beacon light [Had to use another default tower that had a built-in beacon attached and inserted it inside this one as the one I added from the sim was not showing for some reason?]
L72:   * - Added Airport lights around the airport to give it some life at night.
L73:   * -  Added extra lighting under and above the Airport terminal roofing that was added and around the sides.
L74:   * - Added static aircraft\service vehicles with some animated Marshalls surrounding them.
L75:   * - Randomly placed Marshalls and other animated people around the Airport in general.
L76:   * - Added barbwire fencing around entire Airport, including a concrete wall that's South of the control tower that's literally built from a single brick :)
L77:   * -  Added many more trees/plants/grass, auto-gen trees in general areas close to and surrounding the Airport
L78:   * - Added 1 boat where they are usually located at by the dock. [Work in progress]
L79:   * - Added street lights to light up the road and additional lamp posts with lights along the Northern side of the runway.
L80:   * - Added the approach red lights behind runway 10
L81:   * - Cleared default parking lot behind terminal building to recontruct it [work in progress]
L82: DETAILED UPDATED FEATURES TO DEFAULT SCENERY (V1.0) - TKPK:
L83:   * - Started from scratch and deleted everything except the default terminal building.
L84:   * - Still havn't used Blender in very long while, so I stratigically placed very specific scenery objects from the sim library around the default building to try and match the design structure IRL :)
L85:   * - Made some corrections to the surrounding terrain of the Airport and raised "Booby Island". MSFS had it flat by default  (The extremely tiny island in the channel between St.Kitts and Nevis)
L86:   * - Added runway/lights, PAPI lights, aprons, taxi lights, taxi signs, taxi ways, textures and ground markings. (The parking names/letters and taxi sign letters may not be accurate so I just used my imagination)
L87:   * - Corrected location of Windsock and added the small red and white checkered building next to it
L88:   * - Added the control tower with a beacon light (Had to use another default tower that had a built-in beacon attached and inserted it inside this one as the one I added from the sim was not showing for some reason?]
L89:   * -Added the Airport's solar panels near the runway and removed the auto generated buildings that were in their place.
L90:   * - Replaced the default building they had as the hanger which is normally on the East apron with one thats close enough to the real thing (in shape and color that is)
L91:   * - Added Airport lights around the airport to give it some life at night.
L92:   * - Added extra lighting under the Airport terminal roofing that was added
L93:   * - Added static aircraft\service vehicles with some animated Marshalls surrounding them.
L94:   * - Randomly placed Marshalls and other animated people around the Airport in general. (Take the drone and have a look around if you like :-] )
L95:   * - Added barbwire fencing around entire Airport  (and the section of land behind Runway 07)
L96:   * - Added many scenery objects/details/markings to the Airport parking lot to match close to IRL as possible (work in progress)
L97:   * - Added many more trees/plants in general areas close to the Airport
L98:   * - Added cruiseships, boats and docks where they are usually located at sea.
L99:   * - Added tall lights to both Cricket stadiums
L100:   * - Added street lights to light up the Bypass road and Kim Collins Highway and additional lamp posts along the road
L101:   * - Added paved roads to the Bypass road and Kim Collins Highway and some near the Airport (work in progress)
L102:   * - Added extra animated traffic on the bypass road to give it some life. (By default the sim has the US standard traffic rules and not Europe standards which we do adapt IRL) I may add some more later on in areas that are usually busy
L103:   * -Added traffic lights in their current locations around Basseterre (Again, fly around with the drone if you'd like to see them.)
L104:   * - Added the approach red lights behind runway 07 and additional scenery objects to replicate the real life scenery behind there
L105:   * - Added an animated flag where our national flag pole is supposed to be (I'm not sure if everyone can see this or if it's a default in the library. Anyone who can't see it let me know right away)
L106: 
L107: 
L108: Thats all for now. More to come in every version update here. Do enjoy this on going project which took a great deal of time and effort. Feel free to leave any comments after you've flown around. Have fun flying and see you in the Sim world :)

L24: ### Description L25: Welcome eveyone to the first vabb airport of msfs. Myself Abhijit Anil. This is my first ever airport work so i started with my home airport.Aviation in the Mumbai region dates back as far as 1932, when mail planes used the Juhu air strip, less than 3 miles / 2 km from the actual site of the city's airport today. In 1940, Mumbai decided to find an alternative site and a spot was chosen at Santa Cruz and Chhatrapati Shivaji Airport was born. L26: Used by the military during the war years, Mumbai Airport was managed by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation from 1946 onwards and in 1958, a new terminal was opened. L27: In 1972, the operation of Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (BOM) was taken over by the International Airports Authority of India and expansion plans were soon implemented over the next three decades. By the turn of the new millennium, the airport had grown to become the busiest in the whole of India. L28: Both the domestic and the international terminals at Mumbai International Airport offer extensive passenger and visitor facilities. These services include cashpoint machines, exchange desks and postal services throughout, while snack bars and restaurants provide sustenance, along with a series of vending machines. Duty-free shopping is also available, together with left luggage facilities in both terminals, medical services, quiet rooms, a Telecom centre, television screens and child care rooms. L29: Business centres and executive lounges are available at Mumbai Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport for the exclusive use of business-class passengers. Conference facilities are to be found at the nearby Leela Kempinski Hotel, with is less than 1 mile / 1.5 km away and can be reached in minutes. L33: 3) Made Boundary and reworked on the surrounding area L34: 4) Accurate ground detailing L35: 5) taxi signs and taxi way are assigned according to real world chart. L36: 6) Wind sock position accurate to real world. L37: 7) All ground vehicles will follow service path instead of taxi line L38: 8) All GA aircrafts have given a separate location in the airport with small hangars next to it. L39: 9) All Cargo Plane have given a separate location in the airport with cargo hangars in front of it. L23: Nouakchott Oumtounsy Airport GQNO
L24: ----------------------------------------------------
L25: Nouakchott–Oumtounsy International Airport (IATA: NKC, ICAO: GQNO) is the new international airport serving Nouakchott, the capital of Mauritania , located 25 kilometres (16 mi) north of the city.
L26: The airport opened in June 2016 as the replacement for Nouakchott International Airport which was located in the city
L27: Egis Group put in place the airport transfer program, which saw the simultaneous shut down of the previous airport and opening of the new airport to the public on the same day

L23: 
L24:           I almost abandoned this project when Asobo released World Update XIII. Their version of PHKO has a lot to offer. Nevertheless, some people might like to see a different version. My latest update brings some things into alignment with the latest aerial imagery, and fixes a few shortcomings of my original release.
L25: The airport: Ellison Onizuka Kona International Airport at Keahole (PHKO) is one of two international airports located on the island of Hawai’i. PHKO is located on the leeward side of the island, while Hilo International is located on the windward side.
L26:             The airport has gone through a number of name changes since its construction in 1970. The current name honors Kona native Ellison Onizuka, an astronaut who died in the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster of 1986. “Keahole” refers to Keahole Point, the projection of land created by the lava flow of 1801.
L27:             A modernization project began in 2017. The project included the creation of a centralized security checkpoint, the construction of a large baggage facility, and the demolition of the Onizuka museum and the old tower.
L28: 
L29:             I am grateful to polyhaven.com, ambientcg.com, and pexels.com for their assortment of royalty-free textures and images.
L30: 
L31:             I am also grateful to Patrick Germain for his airport2project app, which helped me create a starting point for this package.
L32: Installation: Unzip, and place the phko-airport-kona folder in your community folder. This airport package is contained in one folder only. If you see more than one phko folder in your community folder, please remove any older versions before launching MSFS.
L33:           Next, you'll need to remove Asobo's PHKO to prevent overlapping scenery elements. Launch MSFS. From the main menu, go to "Profile." From there, go to "Content Manager." Search for Asobo's PHKO. I think the easiest way to do that is to use the search window in Content Manager. Type in PHKO, and two items should appear. One is the World Update XIII: Oceania and Antarctica file, and the other is PHKO Airport Kona by Lima Juliet.
L34: Move your cursor over the World Update XIII file, and a blue rectangle should appear to the right, with a set of dots and lines that look like a bulleted list. Left click on the blue rectangle, and the components of WU XIII will be revealed. Select the "PHKO KONA AIRPORT" entry, and then click on the "Delete" option at the bottom of the screen.
L35:           If you grow weary of my version of PHKO and want to put it back the way it was, it'll entail a two-step process similar to the one above. In addition to removing my package from your community folder, you'll need to reinstall Asobo's version. From the main menu in MSFS, go to "Profile," and then to "Content Manager." Search for Asobo's PHKO, as above. Open the World Update XIII file again, and select "PHKO KONA AIRPORT." This time, an Install option will come up at the bottom of the screen.

L23: 
L24: Cairns Airport (ICAO: YBCS) is an international airport in Cairns, Queensland, Australia. Formerly operated by the Cairns Port Authority, the airport was sold by the Queensland Government in December 2008 to a private consortium. It is the seventh busiest airport in Australia. The airport is located 2.3 nautical miles (4.3 km; 2.6 mi) north northwest of Cairns in the suburb of Aeroglen. The airport lies between Mount Whitfield to the west and Trinity Bay to the east.

L37: History
L38: 
L39: 1936 - The Cairns City Council bought 162 hectares of land and built three runways made of cinders, red earth, weathered rock and sand.
L40: 1937 - The Australian Government bought the airport during World War II for use by the Royal Australian Air Force. The Main runway was sealed and made longer for the RAAF aircraft.
L41: The airport has direct flights to 7 international and 17 domestic destinations and many general aviation flights including a number of helicopter operators. Flights are operated to all major Australian cities and tourist destinations, regional communities in Far North Queensland, and a number of international destinations in the Asia-Pacific region, with connections to the rest of the world.
L42: The airport formed the main base for Australian Airlines prior to its ceasing of operations in June 2006 (the airport remains a major port for parent company Qantas). It is also a base for the Royal Flying Doctor Service of Australia and the search and rescue helicopters of the Queensland Government. In the 12 months ending 30 June 2019 Cairns Airport had just over 5 million passengers.

L23: 
L24: Update 0.7.6
L25: 
L26: This update is especially for anyone who plays with vanilla Ai ATC.
L27: 
L28: Fixed no-giving Military Stands for Fighters.
L29: Fixed apron and taxiways.
L30: 
L31: But, You will still need to edit 'aircraft.cfg' file to get Military Stands.
L32: Or you can download it instantly from the link: cite33†MEGA†mega.nz for FA-18e
L33: Want to watch what I did? :) cite34†MSFS | Airport Upgrading | VYYY Yangon Intl Airport | Myanmar Airports - Part 3 - YouTube†www.youtube.com L34: Update 0.7.4
L35: Re-designed some things for the whole airport.
L36: Excluded the trees near Apron B. (near B3 taxiway).
L37: Added painted area at the gates.
L38: Added Runway center lights.
L39: Added Runway lights at the runway end.
L40: Added more fences. :) around the airport.
L41: Added 9 gates number signs at the front of the gates by using taxiways signs.
L42: Added Gate Stands T offsets.
L43: 
L44: Fixed there is no taxiway line at runway 21.
L45: Fixed some bugs.
L46: Fix military taxiways to get ribbon when you play vanilla. (Still not yet test)
L47: Changed Runway Approach lights to SALS.
L48: Changed Runway Edges Light to High.
L49: Replaced the taxiways edge and center lights by custom sketching (Looks clear than before)
L50: Cleaned unnecessary things... to look better.
L51: 
L52: Looks better :)
L53:

L23: 
L24: Read installation instructions carefully. Glass jetways require GSX Pro and use of optional GSX Pro version.
L25: 
L26: Muscat International Airport, formerly Seeb International Airport, is the main international airport in Oman. The airport serves as the hub for flag carrier Oman Air and Oman's budget airline Salam Air, and features flights to several regional destinations as well as intercontinental services to Asia, Africa and Europe.
L27: The entire airport has custom 3D models and textures. Runway 08R/26L has been closed as in real life. The layout is accurate and current as of August 2022.
L28: 
L29: * * *
L30: 
L31:  INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS
L32: 
L33: If you don't have GSX Pro:
L34: 
L35:   * Open the "Default Jetways Version" folder.
L36:   * Move "qnh997-muscat-intl" into your Community folder.
L37: 
L38: If you have GSX Pro:
L39:   * Open the "GSX Version" folder.
L40:   * Move "qnh997-muscat-intl" into your Community folder. If you install the GSX version, do not install the main file - choose one or the other.
L41:   * A GSX profile can be found in the "GSX Version" folder. Copy and paste this in "%APPDATA%\Virtuali\GSX\MSFS". The GSX profile covers all North Civil (i.e. new terminal) and Cargo aprons.
L42:   *  Make sure OOMS is disabled in the Jetway Configuration section of your GSX settings (which can be accessed via the FSDT Installer).
L43: * * *
L44: 
L45: OPTIONAL HIGH RES AERIAL IMAGERY
L46: 
L47: An optional color corrected high res aerial imagery file has been included. I kept this seperate for those who want to minimize the file size of the package, but highly recommend installing it as it makes the ground look much crisper.
L48: 
L49:   * Open the "Aerial Imagery OPTIONAL" folder.
L50:   * Move "ek1288-ooms-aerial" into your Community folder".
L51: 
L52: * * *
L53: 
L54: KNOWN ISSUES
L55:   * The airport's old name still shows in MSFS's menus. This a sim limitation, airport names in the menus cannot currently be changed.
L56:   * Floating/"disconnected" jetways is a sim issue, not a scenery issue.

L28: Cam Ranh International Airport (IATA: CXR, ICAO: VVCR) (Vietnamese: Sân bay Quốc tế Cam Ranh) is located on Cam Ranh Bay in Cam Ranh, a town in Khánh Hòa Province in Vietnam. It serves the city of Nha Trang, which is 30 km (16 NM) from the airport. This airport handled 9,747,172 passengers in 2019,[1] making it the fourth busiest airport in Vietnam, after the ones in Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi and Da Nang, and one of the fastest growing airports in the country.
L29: This is the only airport in Vietnam that handles more international passengers than domestic passengers, with international passengers accounting for 70% in 2018.[2] It is the fourth busiest airport in Vietnam.
L30: 
L31: Cam Ranh Terminal 1 is used for domestic flights and Cam Ranh Terminal 2 (managed by Cam Ranh International Terminal (CRTC) JSC) is used for international flights.

L27: 
L28: Daniel K. Inouye International Airport, formerly known as Honolulu International Airport, is the largest international airport in the state of Hawaii, U.S.A. It is located on the island of Oahu, west of downtown Honolulu.
L29: This package adds two towers designed to more closely resemble the real-world towers at PHNL. The package also adds the breezeways between the main terminal building and the C and G concourses, the open-air gates extending east from the G concourse, the Mauka concourse, the HAL maintenance and cargo buildings, the ARFF building on the north side of runway 8L/26R, the United maintenance hangar, and a few other items here and there.
L30: I used a generic apartment building from the Asobo library as a stand in for the FDC building.
L31: In addition to adding the above objects, I also added some helipads. I changed the gate names at the terminal to PHNL's current alphanumeric system, and I also renamed some of the taxiways to match the present-day taxiway names. And of course, I replaced most of the default painted lines with custom painted lines.
L32: I'm hoping to release updates with additional objects and custom terminal buildings. And I plan to add seaplane parking soon. I would've included the latter with the initial release, but I became discouraged by the fact that I couldn't get my "dock_GA" parking to interact properly with ATC, so I deleted it. Still, I really want to be able to spawn a cold-and-dark seaplane out in the water, so I'll probably add the dock_GA back in, whether it plays well with ATC or not.
L33: To install, unzip the downloaded file, and place the unzipped lmj-airport-phnl folder into your community folder.
L34: 
L35: I thank ambientcg.com, polyhaven.com, and pexels.com for their royalty-free textures and images. And I thank the security officers at PHNL for not stopping me last November to ask why I was spending three hours inside their airport, photographing everything from departure/arrival boards to restroom signage.

L249: # MBPV-Providenciales International Airport + Executive terminal
L250: ovidenciales International Airport (IATA: PLS, ICAO: MBPV), on the island of Providenciales in the Caicos Islands, is the main international airport serving the Turks and Caicos Islands, a British Overseas Territory of the United Kingdom. It is operated by Turks and Caicos Islands Airports Authority (TCIAA). The territory's other international airport is JAGS McCartney International Airport on Grand Turk Island. Currently, there are more than 12,000 commercial aircraft operations per year.

L23: 
L24: Welcome to Faleolo Airport in Apia, Samoa. I've been dropping things onto the island for a week now. Cars, trucks, luggage, airplanes, people, animals, even buildings. Then I flattened the whole area. Now let's give the Samoans a little rest.
L25: Hope you enjoy this rendition of the airport. It's designed with library objects you need some phantasy but if you've never been there, you won't even recognise. Check out all the little detail including some turtles and birds on the coast. This mod includes the latest airport layout with the regional terminal that was opened in 2024.
L26: 
L27: This scenery has evolved over many updates. It's now a fully working airport with lots of detail, wildlife and fun stuff. Enjoy!

L24: Description:
L25: Experience the vibrant atmosphere of N’Djili International Airport (FZAA), located just 24 kilometers from the heart of Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo. This airport serves as the main hub for travel across Central Africa and beyond, connecting Kinshasa to key destinations in Africa, Europe, and the world. A big thank you to Maya for crafting the stunning custom buildings, which bring this airport to life in Microsoft Flight Simulator.
L26: Every detail has been carefully designed to create an authentic and immersive experience for virtual pilots.
L27: Fly the skies of Central Africa and discover the beauty of the Democratic Republic of Congo with this detailed rendition of N’Djili International Airport! Download now and take off from the heart of Kinshasa
L28: 
L29: Features:
L30:   * Custom-Built Terminal Buildings: Faithfully recreated to reflect the unique architecture of FZAA.
L31:   * Realistic Layout: Enjoy accurate runways, taxiways, and apron areas for a seamless experience.
L32:   * Strategic Location: As the main gateway to Kinshasa, FZAA offers stunning views of the city and the Congo River Basin.
L33:   * Dynamic Lighting: Experience immersive night flying with beautifully rendered airport lighting.
